answer: A mechanism that actually bites: bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because reef only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. In practice juniper is enforced by the ledger itself: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any cipher approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
